intro: Malaysia is split in two by the South China Sea: Peninsular Malaysia on the mainland, and Sabah and Sarawak on the island of Borneo.

chapters.title: Two halves
text: Peninsular Malaysia has a mountainous spine, the Titiwangsa range, with cool hill stations like the Cameron Highlands. East Malaysia, on Borneo, is larger and wilder, with huge rivers and rainforest.
Mount Kinabalu in Sabah, 4,095 m, is the highest mountain in the country.

chapters.title: Rainforest and wildlife
text: Malaysia's rainforests are among the oldest on Earth, home to orangutans, proboscis monkeys, hornbills and the giant rafflesia, the world's largest flower. Much forest has been cleared for oil palm plantations.
The Mulu caves in Sarawak include one of the largest cave chambers in the world.

chapters.title: Climate
text: Malaysia is hot and humid all year, with monsoon rains that flood the east coast from November to February.
